kyoto_gion_yutaka_steak.gf_detail: Ask. Courses pair the steak with carpaccio, soup, salad with house dressing, garlic rice and bread; the steak itself is steamed on garlic on the griddle; no gluten information (official site; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_gion_yutaka_steak.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a steakhouse whose courses centre on wagyu fillet, with seafood starters (official site).
kyoto_gion_yutaka_steak.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–13:30 (last order); dinner from 17:30 (Tabelog lists 17:30–22:30, last order 22:00); closed Sunday and public holidays, and irregularly (Tabelog; official site). Reservation only (Tabelog), by phone or TableCheck (official site). Lunch steak course ¥8,800; dinner courses from ¥32,000; prices include service and tax (official site). 24 seats: a 10-seat counter facing the kitchen and a small garden, a private room for 6, and an upstairs zashiki with a stage for parties with geiko and maiko (official site; Tabelog). Non-smoking; cards accepted (Tabelog). Gion Machi Minamigawa, south of Shijo off Hanamikoji; about 10 min from Gion-Shijo Stn (Tabelog). Moved here from 末吉町 on 7 May 2012 (Tabelog).
kyoto_gion_yutaka_steak.notes: [Steak · Gion, a 1962 steakhouse in a former teahouse] A Gion steakhouse in a remodelled ochaya south of Shijo, entered under a noren and red lantern, with a vermilion counter that faces the griddle and a small garden. The house steak is the heart of the black wagyu fillet, cut thick and steamed slowly over garlic so it is soft enough to barely need chewing; it comes with garlic rice and a triangle of pudding. The lunch course (¥8,800, 80 g fillet) is the way in; dinner courses start at ¥32,000. Upstairs there is a zashiki with a stage for parties with geiko and maiko. Reservation only; closed Sunday.

chef_bio.chef_name: Mamoru Takada (official site; the kanji is not given)
roles: Second-generation owner-chef (official site: 二代目オーナーシェフ)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: Steak House Yutaka was founded in 1962 (Showa 37); following the founder, the father, Takada entered cooking after high school, was put in charge of the Gion shop at 24 and became owner young; the father's teaching "cooking is conversation" is kept; the company also runs Yutaka Ginza in Tokyo. A June 2025 review gives the owner-chef's name as "Ei Takada"; a September 2026 review (in Japanese) gives 創業62年 and saw the owner and one young cook running the room. A June 2026 reviewer says Kazuo Inamori and family were regulars in the founder's time. Tabelog Steak WEST "Tabelog 100" 2022, 2024 and 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: the joy of food that comes out of conversation — reading each guest and recommending what suits that day, from the composition of the meal to the doneness of the meat.
chef_bio.specialty: Steamed black wagyu fillet (Chateaubriand); garlic rice.

anecdotes.text: A September 2026 lunch guest (writing in Japanese) found the room to be a business-entertaining restaurant of an older era, run that day by the owner and one young cook, and had the ¥8,800 lunch course.
A June 2026 diner had 150 g of Chateaubriand while a companion over 70 ordered 300 g and finished it.
A March 2026 regular of about ten years booked the second-floor private room for a group of eight.

kyoto_ristorante_noro.vegan_detail: Ask. Courses centre on fish, meat and egg pasta; the seasonal vegetable plate is the most plant-based dish reviewed, but its jelly is set with a dashi broth (2026 reviews).
kyoto_ristorante_noro.hours_raw: Tuesday–Sunday 11:30–13:30 and 17:30–20:30; closed Monday; hours may change (Tabelog). Reservations taken; lunch fills up, so book (Tabelog; July 2026). Lunch: menchi-katsu set ¥3,300 (August 2026); lunch course with soup, fish tasting, pasta, main, dessert and drink. Dinner course ¥10,000 (¥11,000 with tax) (October 2026); à la carte at night has no printed prices (July 2026). 12 counter seats on the ground floor (10 per an August 2026 review), with tables upstairs and in a separate building; non-smoking; JCB, AMEX and Diners only (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). 8 min from JR Nijo Stn; no parking (Tabelog). Opened 13 June 2017 (Tabelog).
kyoto_ristorante_noro.notes: [Italian yoshoku · Nijo, a menchi-katsu worth the trip] A renovated machiya a short walk from JR Nijo Stn where chef Noro — trained in Italy, then at Hotel Granvia Kyoto's La Risata and at Yoshoku Ogata — cooks Italian-based yoshoku with Japanese touches. The signature is a juicy menchi-katsu of Ozaki beef and Kofuku pork under demi-glace and balsamic; the menchi-katsu lunch set (¥3,300) comes with a soup and a vegetable plate that reviewers rave about. Dinner is a ¥10,000 course or à la carte with handmade pasta, risotto and the day's fish. Lunch fills up — book. Closed Monday.

chef_bio.chef_name: Noro (surname only; owner-chef per July and August 2026 reviews)
roles: Owner-chef (July 2026 review: "Chef Noro, the owner"; August 2026: "The owner, Mr. Noro")
chef_bio.background: Per a July 2026 review: chef Noro trained in Italy, then worked at Hotel Granvia Kyoto's La Risata and at Yoshoku Ogata before opening Ristorante Noro in 2017 (Tabelog: 13 June 2017). The official site describes the shop as a kappo-like restaurant that serves "100 dishes for 100 guests", for ordinary days and special ones. Tabelog Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021 and 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: 「100人の方に、100様の料理でもてなす、割烹のようなレストラン」 — a restaurant like a kappo, serving each guest a dish made for that guest.
chef_bio.specialty: Menchi-katsu with demi-glace and balsamic; handmade pasta.

anecdotes.text: An August 2026 diner was seen off at the door by the owner, Mr. Noro, and found the welcome very friendly and warm.
An August 2026 regular, on a second visit, wrote at length about the chilled corn soup of Dake Kimi corn and a vegetable plate of beets, apple and blood-orange jelly set with dashi.
An August 2026 diner asked for both a seafood and a summer-vegetable risotto, and the kitchen made one with cream and one with tomato.

kyoto_hassunba_pontocho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice for overseas guests: the shop offers them only a fixed course that includes fish tempura and miso-grilled fish (Tabelog). The à la carte menu adds fried nama-fu (wheat gluten) and dishes in white miso (2026 reviews).
kyoto_hassunba_pontocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the course for overseas guests is an appetiser platter, chicken and root-vegetable soup, fish tempura and miso-grilled fish (Tabelog), and the cooking is built on dashi (October 2026).
kyoto_hassunba_pontocho.hours_raw: Tabelog: every day 17:30–22:30 (last order 22:00), closed irregularly. Bookings taken; a booking more than 15 minutes late without notice is cancelled (Tabelog). For overseas guests the shop offers only a course of four dishes chosen by the owner — appetiser platter, chicken and root-vegetable soup, an original fish tempura and miso-grilled fish, changing with the season — at ¥7,500 including tax; there is no English menu and the owner cannot explain the dishes in English (Tabelog). Table charge ¥1,000 with an appetiser (Tabelog). 18 seats: 6 at the counter, 12 at tables; non-smoking; children and folded strollers welcome (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, AMEX, Diners), no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Down 21番路地 off Pontocho north of Shijo; 5 min walk from Keihan Gion-Shijo Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_hassunba_pontocho.notes: [Kyoto cooking · Pontocho, a hidden alley] A calm 18-seat counter-and-table restaurant at the end of an alley off Pontocho, which a June 2026 diner heard would mark its 25th year that autumn: obanzai and hassun assortments, fluffy dashimaki, fried nama-fu salad, beef and Kujo leek in white miso, and a deep sake list. Overseas guests are offered only a four-dish course (¥7,500), because the owner cannot explain dishes in English. One March 2026 diner found the food bland, greasy and over-seasoned; most others loved it. Daily 17:30–22:30.

roles: Owner (unnamed), who chooses the course for overseas guests
chef_bio.background: Tabelog’s notes for overseas customers say there is no English menu, the owner cannot explain the dishes in English, and foreign guests are offered only a ¥7,500 course of four dishes recommended by the owner. A June 2026 diner, on a fourth visit, heard the restaurant would celebrate its 25th anniversary that autumn.
chef_bio.specialty: Obanzai and hassun; dashimaki; beef and Kujo leek in white miso.

anecdotes.text: "The dashimaki tamago (Japanese rolled omelette) with a 3-minute shelf life was incredibly fluffy and delicious." — July 2026.

A March 2026 diner who walked in found the beef with burdock and lotus root "bland and mushy", the fried dishes greasy and the omelette over-seasoned; four dishes with a beer and a highball came to ¥8,500.
"I hear they will celebrate their 25th anniversary this autumn!" — June 2026.

kyoto_bistro_petit_lapin.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information. Courses come with house rye bread and the dinner menu includes crêpes, pâtés and tarte Tatin; dishes are chosen from a long list, so ask before ordering (official menu; 2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_bistro_petit_lapin.vegan_detail: Ask. No vegan information. Salads (mushroom, Niçoise, carrot râpé) are on the menu, but the bistro cooking leans on charcuterie, pâtés, game and foie gras (official menu).
kyoto_bistro_petit_lapin.hours_raw: Official site: lunch 12:00–15:00 (last entry 13:30); café and dessert 14:30–17:30 (last order 16:30); dinner 18:00–23:00 (last entry 21:30); closed Wednesday plus one run of days off a month, posted on the site. Tabelog gives lunch 12:00–15:00 (food last order 13:30) and dinner 18:00–22:30 (food last order 21:30; courses 21:00), closed Wednesday. Bread and amuse-bouche ¥700 per person (Tabelog). Corkage ¥2,000 for one bottle per two guests; please do not use mobile phones in the room (Tabelog). From January 2026 children are welcome by booking by the day before, with a lunch course or a dinner main (official site); Tabelog still says no children. 15 seats: 5 at the counter, 10 at tables; non-smoking; private hire up to 20; English menu (Tabelog). Cards and e-money (Tabelog). On Gokomachi-dori north of Ayanokoji — one minute south on the street west of Fuji Daimaru; red fence and black sign; 5 min walk from Hankyu Kawaramachi Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_bistro_petit_lapin.notes: [French bistro · Gokomachi-Ayanokoji, a little rabbit] A 15-seat bistro behind a red fence south of Fuji Daimaru, open since July 2009, whose site likens its guests to a hungry little rabbit: French regional home cooking with French wines — lunch courses at ¥3,000 and ¥4,000, a ¥5,500 dinner menu and about 70 à la carte dishes from escargots and boudin noir to Hino venison crépinette with foie gras, and tarte Tatin. Reviewers in 2026 praise the owner-chef's warm service. Closed Wednesday; café hours 14:30–17:30.

roles: Owner-chef (unnamed), per 2026 reviews
chef_bio.background: The official site describes a shop where people who love to eat gather, always smiling like a rabbit that never stops munching, and serves house "a little rye" bread. A May 2026 diner found the owner-chef attentive and was photographed by the owner on leaving; another the same month found the owner kind.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: a shop where food-lovers gather, never without a smile, like a hungry little rabbit.
chef_bio.specialty: Venison crépinette with foie gras; tarte Tatin; regional French dishes.

kyoto_cucina_italiana_todo.gf_detail: Ask when booking. No gluten information; the lunch courses are built around pasta (three kinds in one course, dried and handmade) with house ciabatta and focaccia and a cream croquette amuse (2026 reviews).
kyoto_cucina_italiana_todo.vegan_detail: Ask when booking. No vegan information; courses use fish, pork, beef, chicken-liver mousse and cheese, with plenty of Kyoto vegetables in the antipasto (2026 reviews).
kyoto_cucina_italiana_todo.hours_raw: Tabelog: lunch 12:00–15:00 (food last order 14:00, drinks 14:30), dinner 17:30–22:00 (food last order 21:00, drinks 21:30); closed Thursday and the second and third Wednesdays. Bookings taken; a diner booked the same day in September 2026. Dinner service charge 10% from 3 March 2024 (Tabelog). 18 seats: counter on the ground floor facing a small garden, tables upstairs, private rooms for 4 and 6, private hire up to 20; non-smoking (Tabelog; September 2026). Cards, no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 4 min walk from Marutamachi Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_cucina_italiana_todo.notes: [Italian · south of the Imperial Palace, three pastas] A northern-Italian "adult trattoria" in a renovated 100-year-old townhouse on Higashinotoin, with a counter facing a small garden and quiet rooms upstairs. Lunch is a set course — the ¥3,700 three-pasta course is the draw, dried and handmade side by side; dinner is a prix fixe where half portions let two people try more. Italian WEST Tabelog 100 2021, 2023, 2025. One October 2026 diner found it salty and the welcome cool. Closed Thursday and the 2nd and 3rd Wednesdays.

roles: Chef (unnamed on the sources read)
chef_bio.background: Tabelog’s introduction: a relaxed "adult trattoria" in a traditional townhouse over 100 years old, blending Japanese and Western styles; the ground-floor counter lets guests watch the cooks, the upstairs tables are calm, and the food is Northern Italian regional cooking with fresh ingredients and simple methods, paired with Italian wines. Tabelog Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023 and 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the Mitsubishi Estate town guide: an unpretentious "slightly grown-up trattoria" for relaxing over the season’s flavours.
chef_bio.specialty: Three-pasta lunch course; prix fixe dinner.

anecdotes.text: "They kindly divided everything in half for us, allowing us to enjoy two varieties of both pasta and the main course." — October 2026.

An October 2026 diner found the seasoning a little salty and "didn’t feel much hospitality overall".

kyoto_forni_hotel_the_mitsui.gf_detail: Ask when booking: the hotel asks diners with allergies to tell it beforehand (official site). No gluten information; courses include pasta (Awaji-made casarecce and cavatelli), focaccia, a croissant with cheese and tiramisu, and the oven turns out Roman-style pizza (2026 reviews).
kyoto_forni_hotel_the_mitsui.vegan_detail: Ask when booking. No vegan menu is listed; consultant chef Fumio Yonezawa is the author of a vegan cookbook and works on vegan cuisine (official site), but 2026 courses used beef, chicken, veal, fish, burrata and cheese.
kyoto_forni_hotel_the_mitsui.hours_raw: Official site: breakfast 7:00–10:00, lunch 11:30–14:30, dinner 17:30–21:30 (last orders); Tabelog: open all year. Prix fixe courses: lunch Moderare ¥5,900, Contento ¥8,900, Divertito ¥12,900; dinner Moderare ¥12,000, Contento ¥15,000, Divertito ¥19,000; prices include the 15% service charge and tax (official site). Christmas courses 24–25 December 2026: lunch ¥13,000, dinner ¥22,000 (official site). Booking online (TableCheck) or by phone (+81 75 468 3166); cancellation 50% two days before, 70% the day before, 100% on the day (Tabelog). 105 seats: 99 at tables including 18 on the terrace, a private room for 6 (lunch from ¥12,700, dinner from ¥19,000); non-smoking, with a smoking area in the hotel; children welcome with a kids’ menu; dress casual; parking for 23 cars, two hours free with ¥8,000 spent (official site; Tabelog). Breakfast is a semi-buffet with a Japanese or American main (September 2026, a hotel guest). On the ground floor of HOTEL THE MITSUI KYOTO; 3 min walk from Nijojo-mae Stn exit 2 (Tabelog).
kyoto_forni_hotel_the_mitsui.notes: [Hotel Italian · Nijo Castle, a garden and a kamado oven] The Italian restaurant of HOTEL THE MITSUI KYOTO, opened November 2020: prix fixe courses of Italian and Kyoto ingredients following the 24 solar terms, Roman-style pizza from a kamado-style oven, and a garden in view from every seat, with consultant chef Fumio Yonezawa since 2022. Lunch from ¥5,900, dinner from ¥12,000, service and tax included. Italian WEST Tabelog 100 2025. Polished five-star service; breakfast 7:00–10:00, lunch and dinner daily.

roles: Consultant chef (from July 2022), per the official site
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: born in Tokyo in 1980, Fumio Yonezawa trained at Trattoria Il Boccalone in Ebisu, moved to New York at 22 and became the first Japanese sous chef at the three-Michelin-star Jean-Georges; back in Japan, after serving as executive chef at a Tokyo restaurant, the chef became chef de cuisine at Jean-Georges Tokyo on its opening in 2014; won the US Embassy’s Taste of America competition in 2013 and, in 2015, was the first Japanese chef to receive the Golden Egg at RED U-35; opened the sustainable grill restaurant The Burn in Minami Aoyama in 2018; wrote Vegan Recipes (Shibata Shoten); runs the company NO CODE; and was appointed consultant chef at FORNI in July 2022. Tabelog gives the restaurant’s opening day as 3 November 2020. Tabelog Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: respect for the tradition of handmade dishes, with the 24 solar terms expressed through Italian and Kyoto ingredients.
chef_bio.specialty: Roman-style pizza from the okudosan oven; prix fixe courses.

anecdotes.text: When everyone greeted guests with "Hello!" instead of "Irasshaimase", a September 2026 diner thought it a lovely touch.
"Although I arrived 30 minutes late, they welcomed me without any sign of annoyance" — and wrote a message on a friend’s plate on request, August 2026.
A diner who has come back each autumn for the chestnut afternoon tea found the chestnut flavour weaker than a few years before but the Mont Blanc exceptional — October 2026.

kyoto_takohachi.notes: [Kappo · Takoyakushi, a family counter for Kyoto food and sake] An 11-seat counter behind a noren in the Shinkyogoku arcade area, run by a family — a couple behind the counter — where plain-sounding Kyoto dishes come out exceptionally well: egg tofu with yuzu, kizushi, anago grilled or blanched to order, hamo and uzaku in summer, fried small taro, and roast duck with Worcestershire sauce. kyoto_gion_kawamichi.notes: [Izakaya · Gion, a woman's counter facing the Minami-za] A small second-floor izakaya on Yamatooji opposite the Minami-za, whose lights fill the window at night, run by its woman owner-chef with one helper. kyoto_kasho_mototanaka.notes: [Kyoto Chinese · Mototanaka, egg-white fried rice] A neighbourhood Kyoto-Chinese restaurant by Mototanaka Station, famous for its egg-white ankake fried rice (¥1,100) — moist fried rice under a fluffy, creamy egg-white sauce — and a crisp ankake yakisoba that one regular has ordered for 25 years. Founder 田口 茂雄 was honoured as a Contemporary Master Craftsman (2017) and received the Medal with Yellow Ribbon (2020); after the founder's death in 2021, 田口 弥生 has run the shop with a son. Lunch sets ¥1,300; cash or PayPay. Closed Wednesday and Thursday.

kyoto_honke_tankuma_honten.gf_detail: Ask when booking. Courses include tempura (油物), red-miso soup and dashi-simmered dishes; the shop prepares halal, kosher and vegan courses on request, but publishes no gluten information (official site).
kyoto_honke_tankuma_honten.vegan_detail: A shojin kaiseki of vegetables only, with vegetable dashi and no alcohol or the five pungent roots, ¥22,000 plus 15% service — book two days ahead (official site). The standard kaiseki is built on suppon, fish and dashi.
kyoto_honke_tankuma_honten.hours_raw: 17:00–22:00 (last order 19:30); closed Sunday, the 2nd and 4th Monday and 25 December–6 January, with a calendar of closures on the official site (official site). Tabelog lists Tuesday–Saturday 17:00–19:30. Bookings from one person, up to three months ahead, by phone or TableCheck; vegan menus two days ahead, kosher seven days ahead, some halal menus the same day (official site). 15% service charge (official site; Tabelog). Seven or eight private rooms for 1 to 35 people; kawadoko riverside seating 1 May–30 September, 17:00–22:00, seat fee ¥1,650 (official site). Children’s platter ¥3,000 by booking (Tabelog). English menu; the okami speaks English (Tabelog; official site). Cards (Tabelog). 5 min walk from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn, 7 min from Gion-Shijo Stn (official site).
kyoto_honke_tankuma_honten.notes: [Kaiseki · Kiyamachi, a 1928 ryotei famous for suppon] A sukiya-style ryotei between the Takase River and the Kamo, founded in 1928 by 栗栖 熊三郎 at a five-seat counter and now run by the family's fourth generation, Junichi Kurisu (from September 2026), a sommelier who travelled some 80 countries. The kaiseki is 'monmo' — ingredients served as they are — and its signature is suppon, in the 丸吸 soup or the 丸鍋 hot pot. It was among the first Kyoto ryotei with halal certification (2014) and serves kosher and vegan kaiseki on request. Courses from ¥22,000 plus 15% service; riverside kawadoko in summer. Booking required; closed Sunday.

roles: 4th-generation executive chef and owner from September 2026 (official site)
Sommelier: A.S.I. Sommelier Diploma, WSET Level 3 Wines and Sake, J.S.A. Sake Diploma (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: founded on 13 December 1928 by 栗栖 熊三郎 and 栗栖 フミ子 as a five-seat counter by the Takase River; the name joins 丹 of Tanba, the founder’s home, with 熊 of 熊三郎; moved to the present site in 1954 as たん熊南店 and opened the Kyoto Takashimaya shop the same year; renamed 本家 たん熊 in 1989 (the separate たん熊北店 was founded in 1957); the third generation, Kumasaburo Kurisu (born 栗栖 富滋), took the name in 1991 and is now senior advisor; Junichi Kurisu trained at the tea-kaiseki house 東京 柿傳, joined in 2009 and became the fourth-generation owner in September 2026, having travelled about 80 countries; the okami, Haruko Kurisu, speaks English. Two Michelin stars in the Kyoto/Osaka 2010 guide; one star in the 2024 guide. Halal certification from the Kyoto Halal Council (2014); kosher certification from Kosher Japan (2023).
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: "monmo" cooking — 「もんも」 is Kyoto dialect for "as it is" — drawing out the flavour of carefully chosen natural ingredients without ornament; and food diversity, so that visitors of any faith or diet can enjoy Kyoto cuisine.
chef_bio.specialty: 丸吸 (suppon soup); 丸鍋 (suppon hot pot); うずら饅頭, 玉子宝楽.

kyoto_teramachi_fukuda.vegan_detail: Not vegan: fish, chicken, duck and suppon dishes built on dashi; even the vegetable dishes use dashi or fish (official menu; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_teramachi_fukuda.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–14:00 (last order 13:30) and dinner 17:00–22:30 (last order 22:00); closed Tuesday and Wednesday (official site; Tabelog). Lunch takes no bookings and is cash only (official site; July 2026); queues can form before 12:00 and the saba-zushi can sell out (March 2026). Dinner bookings taken; courses from ¥5,000 by booking, full charge for same-day cancellations (official site). 20 seats (6 at the counter, three tables for 4); non-smoking; no children under junior-high age; no strong perfume; English menu (Tabelog). Cards and cashless at dinner only (Tabelog). On the 2nd floor of えびすテラス on Teramachi south of Bukkoji, opposite the Watts 100-yen shop — walk to the back of the 1st floor and up the stairs (official site). Opened 5 July 2012 as 美碧 and renamed Teramachi Fukuda on 5 June 2020 (Tabelog).
kyoto_teramachi_fukuda.notes: [Izakaya · Teramachi, kappo cooking at izakaya prices] A second-floor room on Teramachi south of Bukkoji, hard to find — through the building and up the back stairs — where owner-chef 福田 竹志, in Japanese cooking since 18, serves kappo-standard dishes the casual izakaya way. Order the sea-urchin-soy onion, the toro-yuba and uni spring roll, a hamo cutlet in summer, and finish with the house saba-zushi; or come at lunch for the saba-zushi and somen set (¥1,500) or the clam ramen. A strong sake list. Lunch is walk-in and cash only; dinner by booking. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday; no children under junior-high age.

roles: Owner and cook (official site: "店主・料理人 福田竹志")
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: in Japanese cooking since the age of 18, aiming to serve kaiseki-style dishes casually, for locals and visitors alike; the menu follows the four phases of a season (走り、旬、名残り) with orthodox technique, "過ぎず、程よく" (not too much, just right). Per Tabelog: opened 5 July 2012 as 美碧 (みどり) and reopened under the present name on 5 June 2020. Tabelog Izakaya WEST "Tabelog 100" 2024.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: "過ぎず、程よく" — the handwork of a kappo with the ease of an izakaya.
chef_bio.specialty: Saba-zushi; steamed onion with sea-urchin soy; suppon dishes.

anecdotes.text: A regular on a ninth visit (May 2026) had hamo with jelly and fried young ayu, and finished as always with the saba-zushi.
A March 2026 diner who arrived ten minutes before opening found the saba-zushi sold out early and the noodle soup weak.
A July 2026 diner asked about a dish listed only with niboshi as a condiment, and the kitchen kindly made it with somen.

kyoto_kashiya_cafe.vegan_detail: Ask. Many plates use cream, cream cheese, ice cream or butter; no vegan items are marked (2026 reviews).
kyoto_kashiya_cafe.hours_raw: 12:00–19:00 (last order 18:00); closed Tuesday; temporary closures on Instagram (Tabelog). No reservations (Tabelog). Photos of the food only — no other photos or video, to avoid disturbing guests (Tabelog; October 2026). 16 seats at tables, front and back rooms, with garden green at the back (Tabelog; October 2026). Cards (AMEX) and QR payments (Tabelog). Takeaway sweets in a showcase at the door (June 2026). kyoto_kashiya_cafe.notes: [Café & sweets · Nijo, wagashi-meets-pastry plates in a machiya] A quiet dessert café in a long, narrow townhouse on Nijo-dori just east of the Kamo River, with garden green at the back. The plates pair a fruit with something unexpected — Amazon cacao and banana, grapes and cream cheese, amanatsu and yomogi, nashi and osmanthus — mixing mochi, uirou and bean paste with crepe and sablé; the anmitsu is the simpler classic. Takeaway sweets in the front case. Photos of the food only. Reviewers praise the drinks; a few found the welcome cool and the house rules strict. 12:00–19:00, closed Tuesday.

roles: No person is named in the sources
chef_bio.background: Opened 12 September 2014 (Tabelog). Tabelog Sweets WEST "Tabelog 100" 2018–2020, Cafe "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2022 and Cafe WEST 2025. A September 2026 reviewer notes it was serving plated desserts before the recent wave of dessert-course shops.

kyoto_rakuan_ayakoji.gf_detail: Ask. A fish-and-dashi izakaya: sashimi with soy, Saikyo-miso grills, tempura, kara-age and simmered dishes; no gluten information is published (2026 reviews).

kyoto_rakuan_ayakoji.hours_raw: 17:30–22:00 (last order 21:30), Monday to Saturday; closed Sunday and holidays; hours may change (Tabelog). Usually fully booked: reservations a must (May 2026). 30 seats with a counter; non-smoking; cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners) (Tabelog). On the west side of Takakura-dori by Ayakoji, a short walk from Shijo Karasuma (November 2025; May and August 2026); 193 m from Karasuma Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_rakuan_ayakoji.notes: [Izakaya · Shijo Karasuma, fish, dashi and sake by Ayakoji] A busy, always-booked izakaya on Takakura-dori near Ayakoji, a few minutes from Shijo Karasuma, where regulars fill the counter. The broth is the star: duck or lotus-root manju in dashi, matsutake and hamo dobin-mushi in autumn; then an eight-kind sashimi platter, sawara or squid in Saikyo miso, hamo tempura, grilled natural eel. Dishes are made to order and fairly priced — around ¥6,000–8,000 a head in 2026 — with a deep sake list. Book ahead. Closed Sunday and holidays.

kyoto_fufu_roho_nishiki.hours_raw: 9:00–18:00 every day; hours may change (Tabelog). Takeaway shop with two seats inside for eating the dengaku (Tabelog; October 2024). In Nishiki Market, east of Fuyacho; 287 m from Kyoto Kawaramachi Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_fufu_roho_nishiki.notes: [Nama-fu · Nishiki Market, a gluten maker from the 1800s] A nama-fu specialist in Nishiki Market, said by reviewers to date from the Tenpō era (1830s–40s), selling fresh wheat-gluten cakes — plain, millet, sesame, mugwort — to take home, plus hot fried nama-fu dengaku with a long-cooked sweet miso to eat on the two stools inside (about ¥750). Cash only; open daily 9:00–18:00.

roles: Operator unnamed in the sources

kyoto_miyagawacho_suiren.gf_detail: Ask when booking. Monthly kaiseki with dashi, soy-based sauces, miso and fried courses; no gluten information (official site; 2025–26 reviews).
kyoto_miyagawacho_suiren.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the kaiseki courses are built on fish, shellfish, dashi and a meat course (official site; 2025–26 reviews).
kyoto_miyagawacho_suiren.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–15:00 (last order 13:30), dinner 18:00–22:00 (last order 20:00); closed Monday (Tabelog; official site). Courses only, changing monthly: lunch 9 dishes ¥10,000, dinner 12 dishes ¥20,000, with tax, 10% service extra (official site). 20 seats: a 10-seat counter facing the kitchen and its okudo (kamado) on the first floor, three private rooms upstairs (Tabelog; official site). Children welcome in private rooms (Tabelog). Cards accepted; non-smoking (Tabelog). 3 min from Gion-Shijo Stn exit 1 (official site).
kyoto_miyagawacho_suiren.notes: [Kaiseki · Miyagawa-cho, behind the Minamiza] A kaiseki restaurant in a townhouse in the Miyagawa-cho geisha district, with a ten-seat counter around the kitchen and its okudo (kamado) downstairs and private rooms above. The courses change monthly — playful seasonal touches like a summer consommé served as "draft beer" — and end with pot-cooked rice and dashimaki, seconds offered. Lunch ¥10,000, dinner ¥20,000 (+10%). There is a sister shop in Tokyo Midtown. Closed Monday.

chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: like water that turns from raindrops into a stream, cooking should flow flexibly with the seasons and the people; so as not to forget the season or the guest, the shop deliberately keeps no signature or famous dishes.

A New Year guest found the atmosphere hushed — "not one for a casual, lively gathering" — January 2026.

kyoto_grill_kodakara.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: omurice and hayashi rice come under a demi-glace sauce, and the menu runs to fried shrimp, chicken katsu and crab-cream croquettes (2026 reviews).
kyoto_grill_kodakara.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the omurice rice holds beef, every main is meat, egg or seafood, and the sauce is demi-glace (2026 reviews).
kyoto_grill_kodakara.hours_raw: 11:30–20:30; closed Tuesday and Wednesday (official site; Tabelog). No reservations: queues of 10–50 people form before the 11:30 opening, with waits of 30–60 minutes; orders are taken in the line, so food arrives as soon as you sit; evenings are often easier (2026 reviews). 33 seats at tables, no shared tables (Tabelog; October 2026). kyoto_grill_kodakara.notes: [Yoshoku · Okazaki, the omurice queue] A retro yoshoku in Okazaki that has drawn queues for decades for one dish: omurice — beefy ketchup rice in a soft omelette drowned in a rich house demi-glace (¥1,540; the small is plenty). Hayashi rice, fried shrimp and crab-cream croquettes are the other favourites. Expect 30–60 minutes in line from before the 11:30 opening; your order is taken while you wait. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

kyoto_isoyama_pontocho.notes: [Japanese counter · Pontocho, course early, à la carte late] An 8-seat L-shaped counter down Pontocho's alley No. 25, where a young owner cooks alone in front of you. kyoto_pontocho_sushi_ishiya.gf_detail: Ask. Omakase courses of sushi with soy sauce, tempura, simmered and grilled dishes and red miso soup; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2023–26 reviews).
kyoto_pontocho_sushi_ishiya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: sushi, sashimi, fish and Kyoto beef courses with dashi-based soups (Tabelog; 2023–26 reviews).
kyoto_pontocho_sushi_ishiya.hours_raw: Lunch 11:00–15:00 by reservation only, dinner 17:00–23:00; closed Wednesday, though Wednesday bookings can be discussed (Tabelog); a March 2025 reviewer says lunch needs booking by the day before. 12 seats at the counter, private rooms for 2–8, private hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Non-smoking; cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) (Tabelog). kyoto_pontocho_sushi_ishiya.notes: [Sushi · Pontocho, at the end of alley 24] A sushi counter hidden at the end of Pontocho's alley No. 24, with fans bearing geisha names on the walls and private rooms behind. Reviewers found the head chef friendly and good company at the counter. Closed Wednesday; enter from the Pontocho side.

roles: Owner and head chef (unnamed in the sources)

Reviewers in 2024 describe a friendly, attentive head chef and a counter decorated with fans bearing geiko names; a June 2023 reviewer recognised the premises as a former restaurant run by an elderly couple.
chef_bio.specialty: Omakase nigiri; Kyoto beef dishes.

"The entrance is from the street in Pontocho, so you can’t access it from the Takase River." — July 2024.

kyoto_gion_morikou.gf_detail: Ask. Cantonese dishes with soy and oyster-type sauces, spring rolls, shrimp tempura, dumplings, yakisoba and kara-age; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_gion_morikou.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork, chicken, shrimp, crab and beef dishes, with a Japanese-dashi accent in some (2026 reviews).
kyoto_gion_morikou.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–14:00 (last order 13:30), dinner 17:00–21:30 (last order 20:30); closed Wednesday and on some other days (Tabelog). Book ahead, especially for lunch: a May 2026 walk-in could not get in, and tables fill within minutes of the 11:30 opening (October 2026); a November 2026 walk-in was given a 45-minute slot. The weekday daily special is weekdays only (October 2026). A 10% charge applies only in the tatami rooms (Tabelog). 37 seats: 20 at tables and rooms with sunken kotatsu; private hire for 20–50 (Tabelog). Non-smoking; cards (VISA, Master) (Tabelog). kyoto_gion_morikou.notes: [Kyoto Chinese · Gion Shirakawa, light Cantonese since 1955] A Cantonese restaurant in a house on the Shirakawa, open since 1955, cooking the light, dashi-tinged Chinese food Kyoto calls its own; inside hangs a large peacock painting by a Kyoto artist. Lunch is the two-tier Morikou bento (¥1,400 in 2026) of spring rolls, shrimp tempura, crab omelette and sweet-and-sour pork; dinner brings shark-fin soup, Peking duck and the handmade spring rolls. Book ahead — lunch fills at opening. One October 2026 diner found the mapo tofu too oily. Closed Wednesday.

kyoto_gospel_ginkakuji.notes: [Café · Ginkakuji, scones in an ivy-covered house] A tea room up a broad wooden staircase on the 2nd floor of an old ivy-covered Western-style house near the Philosopher's Path: dark wood, antique furniture, shelves of worn records, and jazz from a JBL Paragon speaker. kyoto_oden_kappo_kanoya.notes: [Oden · Kiyamachi, oden kappo with dashi-wari] A bright, modern oden kappo on the Kiyamachi side near Bukkoji, which moved here from Gion in 2024. Try the dashi-wari, sake or shochu let down with the broth. A ¥9,000 course or à la carte; ¥700 otoshi. A young, quick staff, Showa-era hits on the speakers, a long counter and two private rooms. Open 16:00–23:00, closed Sunday.

kyoto_osake_to_shokuji_uri.notes: [Japanese · Shijo Kawaramachi, a hideaway at the end of an alley] A small, homely restaurant at the end of a narrow alley just off Shijo Kawaramachi, opened in 2018 by a chef who had been head chef at Nikomi Suzuya. Quiet enough to come alone; good with sake. The chef cooks single-handed, so service can be slow, and some find it pricey for what it is. Closed Monday.

kyoto_madam_koran.vegan_detail: Ask. Seasonal Kyoto-vegetable dishes and vegetable oil are used, but the happosai rests on a Chinese stock and most dishes carry meat or seafood (official site; 2026 reviews).

Reservations taken by phone; often full at lunch (2026 reviews). Lunch: Chinese bento with soup ¥1,600; mini kaiseki ¥3,000, from two people, ordered by 13:30 (October 2026). kyoto_madam_koran.notes: [Chinese · Marutamachi, Kyoto-style Sichuan in a sukiya house] A Chinese restaurant south-east of the Imperial Palace in a 90-year-old all-cypress sukiya house that was the main home of a confectioner: chairs downstairs, tatami rooms up a steep stair. The cooking is Sichuan at heart but gentle, with seasonal Kyoto vegetables four times a year — the Kamo eggplant mapo in summer is a favourite. Lunch is the mini kaiseki (¥3,000, two or more) or a ¥1,600 Chinese bento; reviewers rate the kaiseki and the xiaolongbao well and are cooler on the bento. The Dongpo burger (pork belly in a mantou) also sells as a gift. Book ahead; closed Monday.

roles: Kitchen and owners not named on the official site
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the restaurant occupies a renovated 90-year-old sukiya-style house of solid hinoki that was once the main house of a confectioner; the motto is to serve first the flavours the cook finds delicious, with original recipes. A September 2026 reviewer notes Michelin recognition. Tabelog Chinese WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: 「まず自分が美味しいと思った味覚をお客様に提供する」 — serve the guest, first of all, what one has found delicious oneself.
chef_bio.specialty: Kamo eggplant mapo; Dongpo burger; mini kaiseki lunch.

kyoto_umezono_kawaramachi.gf_detail: Ask. Mitarashi dango, shiratama, warabi mochi and kanten are starch- and rice-based, but the mitarashi sauce is soy-based and baked matcha sweets also appear; no ingredient list is published (official menu; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_umezono_kawaramachi.vegan_detail: Ask. Dango, warabi mochi, zenzai and kakigori with bean paste are mostly plant-based, but cream, ice cream, milk kakigori and parfaits use dairy; no ingredient list is published (official menu).
kyoto_umezono_kawaramachi.hours_raw: 10:30–19:30 every day (Tabelog). The group closed 7–9 January in its New Year notice (official site). No reservations; a short wait at busy times (Tabelog; September, October 2026). At least one item per person; three dango can be ordered with a drink (September, October 2026); hojicha is served free (November 2026). Prices across 梅園 were revised from 1 October 2026 (official site). Cards, e-money and PayPay (Tabelog). Non-smoking; takeaway (Tabelog). kyoto_umezono_kawaramachi.notes: [Wagashi café · Kawaramachi Sanjo, mitarashi dango since the 1920s] A long, narrow tea house on Kawaramachi south of Sanjo, founded in 1927 according to a reviewer, where a pot of mitarashi dango greets you at the door. The dango are small, square and grilled until charred at the edges, under a glossy sweet-soy sauce (¥600 for five); pair them with warabi mochi, anmitsu or, in summer, an Uji kintoki kakigori. Hojicha comes free. Most reviewers love the dango; one from Kanto found the sauce far sweeter than expected. Open daily 10:30–19:30; no bookings.

A September 2026 review dates the shop to 1927. Tabelog Wagashi WEST "Tabelog 100" 2023 and 2026.
chef_bio.specialty: Mitarashi dango; warabi mochi; kakigori.

kyoto_shun_ai_sasaki.notes: [Kyoto cuisine · Teramachi-Bukkoji, dashi and beef] A 20-seat Kyoto restaurant on Teramachi with a counter and two sunken tatami rooms, unusual for setting meat — roast beef, oxtail, beef cheek in white miso — among dashi-led seasonal courses that end with clay-pot rice. Lunch from ¥6,600, dinner about ¥13,500 (2026). Reviewers praise an attentive proprietress and call the room new and spotless. Children from middle-school age only. Lunch and dinner daily; book ahead.

roles: Kitchen (unnamed); a proprietress (女将) looks after the room, per a March 2026 review

kyoto_pontocho_tabakoya.notes: [Obanzai izakaya · Pontocho, old-fashioned and lively] A 20-seat obanzai izakaya on Pontocho, behind a wooden sign reading obanzai: home-style Kyoto dishes such as simmered squid and taro, round-eggplant dengaku, Saikyo-miso black cod and fried shrimp-taro, with hot sake. In autumn, koto ouchi rakugan with bean paste. Waraku (2023) describes a family shop run by the second-generation couple and the third generation. Wagashi WEST Tabelog 100 2023 and 2026. Cash only; 9:00–18:00, closed Sundays and holidays.

roles: Second-generation owner, per Waraku (2023)
chef_bio.background: Per Waraku (September 2023, from its October–November 2021 issue): the shop’s founder went independent from 亀末廣 in the early Showa era; the second generation is 西井新太郎, and the shop is run by a couple in their eighties together with the next, third-generation head, 孝明. kyoto_saryo_yoshitsugu.notes: [Wagashi café · Nishiki, matcha and flower-anko cakes in an 1877 machiya] A tea house in a townhouse built in 1877, thirty seconds from Nishiki Market, with a garden and storehouse at the back and a tatami room upstairs for tea lessons. The star is the 花餡ケーキ: a shortcake under a garden of seasonal flowers piped in white bean paste, which sells out — pre-order it on TableCheck. Staff in kimono; order by touch panel. 10:00–18:00, closed Wednesday.

kyoto_ristorante_dei_cacciatori.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: courses only, built around handmade pasta (tajarin, agnolotti dal plin, fettuccine), bread and pastry desserts; no gluten information is published (2019–26 reviews).
kyoto_ristorante_dei_cacciatori.vegan_detail: Not vegan: Piedmontese courses of meat, game, fish, egg pasta, cheese fonduta and anchovy bagna cauda (2019–26 reviews).
kyoto_ristorante_dei_cacciatori.hours_raw: Tabelog lists lunch 11:30–15:00 (last order 13:00) and dinner 18:00–24:00 (last order 21:00) under "Tue – Thu", and Monday as the closing day (open on holidays); the other days are not stated, and the shop’s own site could not be read (it returned an error), so check before going. Courses only (Tabelog). Bookings taken (Tabelog). 16 seats at four tables for four; non-smoking; cards (Tabelog). On Yamato-oji just north of Shijo; 3 min walk from Keihan Gion-Shijo Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_ristorante_dei_cacciatori.notes: [Italian · Gion-Shijo, Piedmont in a three-table room] A small white room with four tables on Yamato-oji just north of Shijo, where chef Nagata — trained in Piedmont under Cesare Giaccone — cooks Piedmontese courses almost single-handed and the chef's wife runs the room. Expect tajarin and agnolotti dal plin made by hand, bagna cauda, game in season (pheasant, Ezo deer), hazelnut sauces and a Barbaresco to match. Courses only; book ahead. Reviewers describe a calm, unhurried place with opera in the background. Check hours by phone.

kyoto_gion_karoku.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a wagyu yakiniku house; namul, kimchi and salad are on the menu, but courses are built on beef and the soup is beef-bone komtang (Tabelog menu; 2026 reviews).

kyoto_gion_karoku.notes: [Yakiniku · Yasaka, wagyu over charcoal in a 1927 mansion] A charcoal yakiniku house in a 1927 mansion just off Yasaka-dori, where you take off your shoes, sit at a sunken table or in a private room looking onto a tsubo-niwa with stone lanterns and pine, and finish with kakigori in a separate room upstairs. The house specialty is negi-tan shio — wagyu tongue wrapped round hand-chopped Kujo negi — with Yamagata beef yukhoe and strip loin dipped in egg. Courses ¥11,000–25,000, cuts from ¥2,800; lunch from ¥2,500. Reviewers praise the setting and mostly the service; one June 2026 host found it short of expectations, and a May 2026 diner found it slow. Closed Monday.

kyoto_gion_fuji_tempura.notes: [Tempura · Gion, a Ritz-Carlton tempura chef's own counter] An eight-seat tempura counter on a street of old Gion houses, opened in 2020 by Kenji Fujimoto, former head chef of Tempura Mizuki at The Ritz-Carlton Kyoto (one Michelin star three years running). Each piece is fried in first-press safflower oil and served as it comes out: hamo and young ayu in summer, a hamo-and-matsutake roll in autumn, fugu and seko crab in winter, and a sesame tofu with sea urchin. Finish with tendon, ochazuke or egg yolk with caviar. Courses ¥17,600–25,300 plus 10% service; a sommelier pairs wine or sake. No vegan, vegetarian, halal or gluten-free requests. Booking only.

kyoto_stars_n_cacio.gf_detail: Ask. Pasta (fresh spinach noodles, ravioli with chestnut-flour dough), pancakes, toast and tiramisu sit beside risotto, salads and grilled meat; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
kyoto_stars_n_cacio.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options and the shop grows its own herbs, but no vegan dish is named; many dishes use cheese, cream, yogurt or eggs (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_stars_n_cacio.hours_raw: Every day: breakfast 9:00–11:00 (last order 10:30), lunch 11:30–17:00 with only part of the à la carte menu from 14:00, dinner 17:30–22:30 (last food order 21:00, drinks 22:30) (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; children under 10 at lunch only (Tabelog). Dogs welcome on the terrace only, kept on the floor (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). 10% service charge; holiday lunches cost more (Tabelog; September 2026). 56 seats: 28 at tables, 8 at the counter, 20 on the terrace; non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Many staff are from abroad and serve in English and Japanese (September and October 2026). About 5 min walk from Kawaramachi Stn (Hankyu) (Tabelog). Opened 1 September 2020 (Tabelog).
kyoto_stars_n_cacio.notes: [Italian · Kawaramachi, la dolce vita from breakfast] A warm, wood-and-greenery Italian restaurant in a townhouse near Kawaramachi that feels, reviewers say, like being abroad: breakfast of pancakes and granola from 9:00 (¥3,850), lunch courses and handmade ravioli, then dinner of pasta, cheese risotto and duck, with cocktails and Italian wines. Much of the staff is from abroad and speaks English, the owner's dog wanders the room, and dogs are welcome on the terrace. A 10% service charge; no children under 10 at dinner. One September 2026 diner with a table booking was first shown to the terrace.

roles: Owner-chef (September 2026 review), unnamed
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: authentic Italian cooking by a chef who was executive chef at renowned hotels, using fresh ingredients from selected regions and herbs from the shop’s own garden, without additives. Per the official site: Italian food with Japan’s finest seasonal ingredients, aperitivos, cocktails and wine, for Kyoto residents and visitors from Japan and abroad, "in the spirit of la dolce vita". Opened 1 September 2020 (Tabelog). A September 2026 regular heard from the owner-chef about white truffle dishes coming the next month; another reviewer saw the owner’s dog roaming the restaurant.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: a destination where excellent food, culture, music, art and fashion converge, "our own definition of luxury".
chef_bio.specialty: Breakfast pancakes; handmade pasta and ravioli.

anecdotes.text: "Many of the staff members are foreigners, but they are also fluent in Japanese. The owner's dog roams around the restaurant, adding to the comforting ambiance." — September 2026.
"The pancakes were crispy and fragrant on the outside, while being soft and fluffy on the inside." — September 2026.

A September 2026 diner with a table booking was led to a dim terrace and told only the terrace was available; a table was opened on request. The holiday lunch came to nearly ¥10,000 with the surcharge.

kyoto_gion_mikaku.gf_detail: Ask. Teppan steak, grilled shabu-shabu and teppan sukiyaki, finished with garlic rice or Mikaku beef curry; sukiyaki and curry usually involve soy sauce or roux, and no gluten information is given (official menu; 2024–2026 reviews).
kyoto_gion_mikaku.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a beef house; even the lunch comes with beef shigure on the rice and a beef-bone soup (official menu).
kyoto_gion_mikaku.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–14:00 (last order 13:30), dinner 18:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); closed Monday; booking required for both (official site). Tabelog adds that dinner should be booked a day or two ahead. Formal dress: no sandals or patterned shirts in summer; school-age children only, no infants (Tabelog). 16 counter seats upstairs around the teppan, plus a private room for up to 7 (official site; Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) (Tabelog). On Nawate by the Shirakawa, north of Shijo; reached by lift; 5 min walk from Gion-Shijo Stn (official site; Tabelog; December 2025).
kyoto_gion_mikaku.notes: [Teppan steak · Gion Shirakawa, a beef house since 1929] A third-generation beef house on the Shirakawa, where the cooks grill only female wagyu — bought whole, aged and boned in-house — on the teppan in front of a 16-seat counter, with big windows onto weeping cherries in spring and greenery in summer. Steak, grilled shabu-shabu and teppan sukiyaki come together in the ¥30,000 three-way course; the lunch steak starts at ¥5,000 for 100 g. The house began teppan steak after the war at the request of occupation officers. Formal dress; book ahead; closed Monday.

roles: Third-generation owner (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: founded in 1929 (Showa 4) — Tabelog’s shop text gives 1927 — as a gyūnabe house that grew on the founder 三田進太郎’s "太牢油焼"; teppan steak began after the war at the request of occupation officers; the founder, the second generation 三田昌治 and the third generation 三田兼司 have served only the best cuts of female cattle; calves registered by nose print and raised in Sanda, Hyogo, are bought whole and aged and boned in the shop; the centenary falls in 2029. A sister shop, 北新地みかく, is in Osaka (official site; a June 2026 reviewer also mentions it).
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: choose the finest beef, cut it with the best technique and cook it to the best doneness, unchanged since the founder.
chef_bio.specialty: Three-way course of steak, grilled shabu-shabu and teppan sukiyaki.

anecdotes.text: A June 2026 group at the counter called it an honour to have a steak grilled by the chef, and admired the greenery through the large windows.
"At the counter seats, the view through the window resembles a beautiful painting." Two lunches of 200 g and 150 g with dessert and coffee came to about ¥16,000. — December 2025.
An October 2024 visitor took the nine-dish tasting course (¥28,000) of sukiyaki, shabu-shabu and teppan steak, finishing with garlic rice and beef curry.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (mikaku.co.jp): 1929年 (昭和4年) 創業、雌牛の太牢のみ、創業者・三田進太郎、二代目・三田昌治、三代目・三田兼司、牛鍋から始まり「太牢油焼」、戦後に占領軍将校の求めで鉄板焼ステーキ、兵庫県三田市で育った子牛を一頭買いし店内で熟成・脱骨、2029年に百周年、東山区常盤町165番地 (祇園縄手四条上ル車道)、カウンター16席、12:00〜14:00 (L.O. 13:30)・18:00〜23:00 (L.O. 22:00)、予約必須、月曜定休、みかく三種焼コース30,000円、みかく牛ステーキコース (もも150g 26,500円、フィレ150g 38,500円、ロース200g 40,000円)、ランチのみかく牛鉄板ステーキ100g 5,000円〜250g 9,500円、北新地みかく。食べログ: ステーキ・すき焼き、1927年からの老舗、Tajima の若い雌牛 (店舗紹介)、夜は1〜2日前までに予約、ドレスコード、小学生以上、乳幼児不可、カード可。口コミ (2025年12月〜2026年6月、英語): 窓からの白川の眺め、シェフが目の前で焼く、ランチ2人で約16,000円。

cultural_comfort.note: Book ahead (Tabelog or TableCheck); English page on the official site; formal dress; cards accepted.

kyoto_trattoria_leone.gf_detail: Ask. Tuscan trattoria: pasta (dried and homemade), lasagna, crostini, arancini and breaded vegetables in the appetiser platter, bread with meals; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
kyoto_trattoria_leone.vegan_detail: Ask. A vegetable aglio e olio and basil pasta appear as daily pastas, but the appetiser platters mix in tuna, liver, omelette and cheese; no vegan dish is named (2026 reviews).
kyoto_trattoria_leone.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–14:30 (last order 14:00), dinner 18:00–22:00 (last order 21:00); closed Wednesday and the third Tuesday of the month (Tabelog). Book by phone: Tabelog takes one online booking (up to two people) a day and none for Friday to Sunday; lunch booking advised (Tabelog; July 2026). No children below elementary school age (Tabelog). 16 table seats; non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), iD, QUICPay, PayPay and au PAY (Tabelog). English menu; sommelier; takeaway (Tabelog). Ground floor of 京都1号館ビル on Takatsuji west of Muromachi; 5–10 min walk from Shijo or Karasuma stations (Tabelog). Opened 11 November 2007 (Tabelog).
kyoto_trattoria_leone.notes: [Italian · Shijo Karasuma, a small Tuscan trattoria] A 16-seat trattoria south of Shijo Karasuma, open since 2007, with maps and drawings on the walls and cooking straight from Tuscany: an appetiser platter so large it is nearly a meal, spicy carrettiera, homemade pappardelle with wagyu ragù, herb-roasted arista and chicken-liver crostini, with Tuscan wines from about ¥3,000 a bottle. Lunch from ¥1,300 is a bargain and fills up — book by phone. Service is quiet and minimal: reviewers in June and October 2026 found it brusque and unexplained. Closed Wednesday and the third Tuesday. Tabelog Italian WEST 100 2021.

roles: Chef and a server (unnamed in the sources)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: a cozy little Italian restaurant of authentic Tuscan cuisine. Opened 11 November 2007 (Tabelog). Tabelog Italian WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021. Regulars in 2026 praise the value and the portions; two 2026 reviewers describe a quiet server who explains little.
chef_bio.specialty: Tuscan appetiser platter; carrettiera; wagyu ragù pappardelle; arista.

anecdotes.text: "The appetizer portion is incredible... I mean, is this really just an appetizer? It's so much food." — July 2026.
A June 2026 diner found the service brusque, the beef tagliata tough and the card payment handled out of sight with no breakdown, though the pastas had a Tuscan flavour.
"At TRATTORIA LEONE, everything I’ve tried has been delicious and there are no misses, all at reasonable prices." — July 2026.
"The quiet server... quite innovative." There was no explanation of the daily pasta or dessert. — October 2026.

kyoto_the_churrasco_kawaramachi.gf_detail: Ask. Grilled meats carved at the table with sauces, alongside a buffet of bread, curry, pizza, pasta and fried dishes; no gluten information (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_the_churrasco_kawaramachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an all-you-can-eat meat restaurant; grilled vegetables, pineapple and the salad bar are sides (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_the_churrasco_kawaramachi.hours_raw: Monday to Friday 16:00–23:30; Saturday 12:00–23:00; Sunday and holidays 12:00–23:30; last food order 22:30, drinks 23:00 (Tabelog). Two-hour sittings (food last order at 70 or 90 minutes, depending on the course); one drink per person unless you take free drinks (Tabelog). Reservations accepted, same-day welcome (Tabelog). From 12 to 31 December courses cost ¥500 more; a reviewer paid ¥500 extra on a Sunday (Tabelog; October 2026). 100 seats; non-smoking; wheelchair accessible; children welcome, with child prices (Tabelog; October 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay; no service or table charge (Tabelog). Menus in English, traditional Chinese and Korean (Tabelog). 6th floor of Don Quijote Shijo Kawaramachi; 2 min walk from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Stn (Tabelog). Tabelog gives the opening as 1 May 2025; the shop text says May 2023.
kyoto_the_churrasco_kawaramachi.notes: [Churrasco · Kawaramachi, all-you-can-eat Brazilian grill] A big, 100-seat churrasco room on the 6th floor of the Don Quijote at Shijo Kawaramachi, with night views over the city: staff — one reviewer mentions a Brazilian chef — carve skewers of beef, garlic chicken and sausage at the table, with grilled pineapple, cheese bread, a salad bar and a well-liked curry. Two-hour courses run ¥3,990–4,990 (more on Sundays and in late December); there is also an Italian buffet with free drinks for ¥3,500. Good for groups and families. One October 2026 regular found the beef tough and the carving clumsy. Tabelog Asian/Ethnic WEST 100 2026.

roles: Staff who carve at the table; a Brazilian chef per one review (October 2026)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: one of the few churrasco restaurants in Kyoto, with all-you-can-eat and all-you-can-drink courses, wagyu skewers grilled and carved in front of you, and a night view; projector and microphone hire for groups. The operator’s website is will-food.com (株式会社WILL). Tabelog gives the opening date as 1 May 2025, while its shop text says "Opened in May 2023". Tabelog Asian/Ethnic WEST "Tabelog 100" 2026.
chef_bio.specialty: Churrasco skewers carved at the table; grilled pineapple.

anecdotes.text: "This restaurant offers authentic churrasco prepared by a Brazilian chef" — October 2026.

An October 2026 repeat visitor liked the pineapple, mushrooms and chicken but found the beef tough and thick or thin by turns as staff struggled to carve it, and was struck on the neck by a skewer while meat was being sliced.

"In the last 10 minutes of the all-you-can-eat period, I could also order additional servings of my favorite churrasco" — October 2026; the same reviewer noted sauces left in open containers on the table.
"And when you come here, you absolutely must try the... self-service homemade curry!" — October 2026.
